stage_a.note: They deliver the pitch with strong, enthusiastic engagement and frequent smiling.
They show sustained engagement and excitement with the product throughout the presentation.
They are friendly and approachable, though some parts are more focused on the product.

venture.description: A 2-in-1 broom with a built-in vacuum to eliminate the need for a dustpan.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, their ask, and present the Vabroom, a broom with a built-in vacuum.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin volunteers to try the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter says he would like to try it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter comes up to sweep and vacuum the cereal pile while the founders guide him.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori looks closely at the sample provided to her.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks why someone wouldn't just buy a vacuum instead.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor explains it is not meant to replace an upright vacuum, but is for quick cleanups.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks the founders to tell the panel about themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor shares that he is married and has five kids.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes that it's a little bit like the Brady Bunch.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond jokes that this explains the belly weight.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor laughs and agrees with Daymond's joke.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor explains he founded a design firm in 2010 that helps small companies license products, which is how he met John.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: John shares he is a fourth-generation plumber who constantly sees problems and makes solutions, leading to patents.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: John explains Trevor's firm helped him launch an item, and Trevor's firm wanted to pivot to retail with this product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks if the product has taken off already.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor confirms that they have come with sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks for their sales over the last twelve months.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: John answers that they have done $3.1 million in sales in the last twelve months.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori, Daymond and Peter react positively to the impressive sales figures.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks where they are selling the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor answers they sell direct-to-consumer and just started retail at Bed Bath & Beyond, selling out of their online stock.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks about the cost of the product and the margin.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: John answers it is $17 landed, wholesales for $37, and retails for $59.99.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks what the profit was on the $3.1 million in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor answers the profit was about $300,000, which they rolled right into inventory.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if they have anything patent pending or patented.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor confirms they have international patents pending and a design patent issued in the US.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks how it is different from a Dustbuster or a similar handheld vacuum.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor explains they developed it because they hate the dustpan, which is a frustrating pain point.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark agrees, noting that nobody can get everything into a dustpan.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor adds that customer feedback highlighted it as a lifesaver for people with mobility challenges who cannot bend over.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how much they have invested in the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: John answers that he invested $200,000.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori notes there was $100,000 raised on Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor confirms the Kickstarter and adds that it was subsequently self-funded by the company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks if he is getting a piece of the industrial design firm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor explains they shuffled employees from the design firm into this new entity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks if there is a contract between the investment entity and the design firm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor confirms there is a royalty paid to the design firm.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with amusement upon hearing the word royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor clarifies that the royalty is a clean way to pay back the design firm for its initial investment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how much that investment royalty is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor answers that the royalty is five percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter asks why they didn't just package the whole design firm together for the investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor explains the design firm does other things, but they would entertain offers for it if there is interest.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter counters that otherwise the structure gets very messy.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark explains that the complex structure and small equity offered are not worth his time, and he exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Peter states he is not convinced the problem is big enough to reinvent the broom so completely, and he exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond says the small equity ask indicates they just want exposure, not a real partner, and he exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin offers the requested money for a royalty and equity in the design firm to secure his return.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori reacts with surprise to the terms of Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates that his offer is a venture debt deal that gets him paid back.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori says she loves innovation but the competition and patent situation make her uncomfortable, and she exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor confirms the terms of Kevin's offer to make sure they understand the royalty structure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor and John confer briefly about the offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor counters Kevin, asking for double the investment for double the equity, dropping the royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin rejects the counter-offer, stating his original offer is the right fit.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin pitches the value he brings and the success of his other deals to convince them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Trevor accepts Kevin's standing offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin holds up the broom, celebrating the deal and joking about buying it for Barbara.

decisions.note: Exits because the corporate structure is too complicated and the equity offered is too small.
Exits because he feels reinventing the broom is too complicated for the problem it solves.
Exits because the 2.5% equity ask indicates they just want exposure, not a partner.

decisions.terms: $350k for a $3 royalty until $700k is paid, plus 2.5% of the design firm
decisions.note: Offers the requested money with a royalty to secure his return and equity in the parent firm.
Exits due to concerns about competition and the strength of the patent.
Counters by asking for double the investment for double the equity, without the royalty.
Rejects the counter-offer, keeping his original standing offer.
